passages.text: And truly we tell you, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than to persist in the place of disobedience: first, because you did not recognize for yourselves what was reasonable; second, because, after hearing what concerned us, you did not come to us; third, because even when we came, you disobeyed us. Therefore, out of concern to spare you, we pray without charge that our peace may come upon you. So if you wish to possess this peace, you must eagerly undertake not to do wrong and nobly bear being wronged—something human nature could not endure unless it first received knowledge of what is beneficial above all, namely, knowledge of the righteous nature of the one who surpasses everything: that, in avenging those who are wronged, he exacts punishment and forever benefits those who act reverently.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to persist in the place of disobedience
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative can mark that in which one continues. “Place” is retained literally, though “state of disobedience” is a viable contextual alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what concerned us
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase denotes matters relating to the speakers without specifying whether these are their circumstances, message, or claims.

lexical_decisions.chosen: we pray without charge
lexical_decisions.rationale: προῖκα conveys acting gratis or without payment. “Freely” is possible but could misleadingly suggest only willingness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ μὴ ἀδικεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι καὶ τὸ ἀδικεῖσθαι γενναίως φέρειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: undertake not to do wrong and nobly bear being wronged
lexical_decisions.rationale: The two articular constructions contrast refraining from wrongdoing with enduring wrongdoing received from others.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what is beneficial above all
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase describes the benefit as preeminent; “supremely advantageous” would be a more formal alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in avenging those who are wronged, he exacts punishment
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐκδικῶν presents him as avenging the wronged, while τιμωρεῖ in this judicial context is rendered as imposing punishment. The latter verb can elsewhere carry the sense of aiding or avenging.

passages.text: Therefore, as right-minded servants of God, recognizing for yourselves what is reasonable, adopt the way of life that pleases him, so that, by loving him in this way and being loved by him, you may possess forever what is beneficial. For he alone has the utmost ability to provide it—he who brought things that did not exist into being, fashioned heaven, compacted the earth, bounded the sea, stored away the things in Hades, and filled all things with air.

lexical_decisions.chosen: right-minded servants of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this exhortation εὐγνώμονες describes people of sound or appreciative judgment. “Grateful” is also possible but is less closely tied to the following recognition of what is reasonable.

lexical_decisions.chosen: adopt the way of life that pleases him
lexical_decisions.rationale: πολιτεία can denote conduct, manner of life, or commonwealth; personal conduct is demanded here.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτῷ γὰρ μόνῳ τὸ παρασχεῖν δυνατώτατόν ἐστιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: he alone has the utmost ability to provide it
lexical_decisions.rationale: The impersonal Greek uses a superlative expression of capacity. The object “it” is supplied from the immediately preceding beneficial thing.

lexical_decisions.chosen: compacted the earth
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb depicts making dense or firmly packed. Renderings involving clay or mud are possible but would make the material more explicit than this wording does.

lexical_decisions.chosen: stored away the things in Hades
lexical_decisions.rationale: ταμιεύω presents the contents as kept or laid up in a store; the neuter plural object is preserved rather than reduced to souls alone.

passages.text: He alone transformed the single, primary, uniform substance fourfold and in opposite directions; then, by mixing them, he made countless blends from them, so that these blends, transformed into opposite natures and mixed together, might produce the pleasure of living through the coupling of opposites. Likewise, he alone created communities of angels and spirits by a nod of his purpose and filled the heavens. He also adorned the visible firmament with stars, for which he marked out paths and appointed a course. He compacted the earth for the growth of crops, but bounded the sea, setting habitation apart in waterless regions. He keeps in store the things in Hades, having named it a place of souls; and he filled all things with air, so that all living creatures might be able to breathe without fear in order to live.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν μίαν καὶ πρώτην μονοειδῆ οὐσίαν τετραχῶς καὶ ἐναντίως ἔτρεψεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: transformed the single, primary, uniform substance fourfold and in opposite directions
lexical_decisions.rationale: μίαν, πρώτην, and μονοειδῆ respectively mark singleness, primacy, and uniformity. ἐναντίως may also be rendered “into opposites.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: countless blends
lexical_decisions.rationale: κρᾶσις denotes a mixture or blending. “Mixtures” is equally possible, but “blends” distinguishes the products from the act of mixing.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through the coupling of opposites
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound denotes counter-pairing or reciprocal conjunction, here involving the previously mentioned opposite natures.

lexical_decisions.chosen: communities of angels and spirits
lexical_decisions.rationale: δήμους literally suggests peoples or organized populations. “Hosts” is possible but would introduce a potentially military nuance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by a nod of his purpose
lexical_decisions.rationale: βουλή may mean counsel, will, or purpose, while νεῦμα depicts an authoritative nod or indication.

lexical_decisions.chosen: setting habitation apart in waterless regions
lexical_decisions.rationale: The clause associates the bounding of the sea with reserving dry places for habitation; no particular inhabitants are named.

lexical_decisions.chosen: breathe without fear
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀδεῶς literally means fearlessly or securely. “Breathe safely” would be more idiomatic but less directly preserve the image.

source_issues.issue: The image-checked selected print places a hyphen immediately before οὐρανούς. It appears to be an editorial or typographical mark rather than part of the word and contributes no defensible lexical meaning.

passages.text: Oh, God’s great and wise hand, which makes all things in all things! For a countless multitude of birds has been brought into being by him, and this multitude is diverse, each bird differing from another in every respect—I mean their colors, beaks, claws, eyes, dispositions, voices, and all the other features. And how many different forms of plants there are, distinguished by countless colors, qualities, and scents! How many animals of the dry land and how many of those in the waters, whose shapes, forms, locations, colors, ways of life, dispositions, natures, and multitude it is impossible to tell! There are also the multitude and heights of mountains, the differences among stones, fearsome recesses, springs, rivers, lakes, seas, harbors, islands, forests, the whole inhabited world, and uninhabited places.

lexical_decisions.chosen: which makes all things in all things
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the repeated πᾶς wording and its broad scope. “Which does everything in every sphere” is a possible interpretive alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον κατὰ πάντα ἐξηλλαγμένος
lexical_decisions.chosen: each bird differing from another in every respect
lexical_decisions.rationale: The singular comparison is distributive within the previously named multitude of birds.

lexical_decisions.chosen: eyes, dispositions, voices
lexical_decisions.rationale: βλέμματα can mean looks, gazes, or eyes; γνώμαι denotes dispositions or traits of mind; φθέγματα denotes uttered sounds or voices.

lexical_decisions.chosen: locations
lexical_decisions.rationale: θέσις literally denotes placement or position. In this catalogue of animal differences, “locations” is cautious; “habitats” or “postures” are possible contextual alternatives.

lexical_decisions.chosen: fearsome recesses
lexical_decisions.rationale: μυχός denotes an inner recess or depth. “Fearsome depths” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: forests
lexical_decisions.rationale: Although ὕλη can mean matter or material, the geographical catalogue supports its concrete sense “woods” or “forests.”

passages.text: And how many other things there are that remain unknown, having escaped human conjecture! But among the things that can be grasped, what human being knows even a single boundary? I mean: how heaven revolves; how the stars move; what forms they have and what constitution of life; what their airy paths are; from where the blasts of the winds are driven about and have their varied operations; from where the springs gush unfailingly, and perennial rivers, coming into being, make their way to the sea, while neither that from which they come is emptied nor that to which they depart is filled; how far the infinite depth of boundless Tartarus extends; on what, then, the heaven that encompasses everything is suspended; how clouds well up out of air and are drawn together into air; what the nature is of thunder, lightning, snow, hail, mist, ice, storms, rain, and hovering clouds; and how that nature molds plants and animals, continually completing them with countless differences and complete precision.

lexical_decisions.chosen: having escaped human conjecture
lexical_decisions.rationale: στοχασμός denotes conjecture, estimation, or speculative inquiry rather than certain knowledge.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν δὲ ἐν καταλήψει ὄντων τίς ἀνθρώπων ἕνα ὅρον οἶδεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: among the things that can be grasped, what human being knows even a single boundary?
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατάληψις concerns apprehension or comprehension, and ὅρος may denote a boundary, limit, definition, or determinate account. The following catalogue favors the broad image of a limit to human knowledge.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what constitution of life
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase attributes a constitution or mode of living to the stars without explaining whether this is literal, cosmological, or analogical; the translation preserves that claim.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ ἀνέμων πνεύματα περιωθεῖται καὶ διαφόρους ἔχει τὰς ἐνεργείας
lexical_decisions.chosen: the blasts of the winds are driven about and have their varied operations
lexical_decisions.rationale: πνεύματα here denotes moving breaths or blasts, while ἐνέργειαι can mean activities, operations, powers, or effects.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μέχρι ποῦ τοῦ ἀπεράντου ταρτάρου τὸ ἄπειρον βάθος
lexical_decisions.chosen: how far the infinite depth of boundless Tartarus extends
lexical_decisions.rationale: The Greek is an elliptical question without an expressed verb; “extends” supplies the minimum required English syntax while preserving both terms of limitlessness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πῶς νέφη ἐξ ἀέρος βρύει καὶ εἰς ἀέρα συντίνεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: how clouds well up out of air and are drawn together into air
lexical_decisions.rationale: βρύω supplies the image of gushing or welling up. The unusual συντίνεται is understood in the contextual sense of being drawn or compressed together; “are condensed into air” is a possible alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τίς φύσις βροντῶν καὶ ἀστραπῶν, χιόνων, χαλάζης, ὀμίχλης, κρυστάλλων, καταιγίδων, ὄμβρων, νεφῶν αἰωρουμένων καὶ πῶς φυτὰ καὶ ζῷα πλάσσει καὶ ταῦτα διαφοραῖς ἀναριθμήτοις πάσῃ ἀκριβείᾳ συνεχῶς ἀποτελουμένη
lexical_decisions.chosen: what the nature is of thunder, lightning, snow, hail, mist, ice, storms, rain, and hovering clouds; and how that nature molds plants and animals, continually completing them with countless differences and complete precision
lexical_decisions.rationale: The feminine participle ἀποτελουμένη most naturally refers back to φύσις, making that nature the agent that forms and completes the plants and animals. A looser attachment to the larger creative process is possible, but the chosen syntax is grammatically defensible.

source_issues.issue: The selected print’s form is orthographically unusual. It may be an itacistic or typographical form corresponding to συντείνεται, but its exact nuance remains uncertain; the surrounding account of clouds nevertheless permits a defensible rendering involving drawing together or condensation.
